reason: 'Shrub or rarely small tree' gives two habits for the whole plant. Frutescent and arborescent habit match. The word 'rarely' only says how often the second one occurs.
The heads sit in racemiform or paniculiform arrays. Raceme-like and panicle-like are the right alternatives for the inflorescence.
The statement is about the leaf blade. 'Adaxially glabrous' means the upper surface is glabrous, so moving the bearer to the leaf lamina adaxial epidermis (PO_0000050) is correct.

fix: In 'X, less often Y or Z', the alternatives go on past the first 'or'. Every listed colour belongs to the relation, so the relation must not stop at the first 'or'.
reason: The flora says 'yellow, less often orange or white'. The relation keeps yellow and orange but drops white, so the set of alternatives is incomplete.

Pistils nearly as long as stamens: length relative to the stamens, about 1:1, marked as approximate. Rubus has many separate pistils, so carpel (PO_0009030) would be more exact than gynoecium. The comparison is still right.
Suborbicular means orbicular with the 'approximately' qualifier.

fix: A hyphenated colour such as 'yellow-red' is one blended colour, like red-brown. Do not reduce it to its last part.
reason: 'Yellow-red' was mapped to plain red (FLOPO_0988001). The other two values, brown and red-brown, are right.

fix: A hyphenated shape such as 'oblong-lanceolate' is one shape between two shapes. It needs both parts or a compound value. It should not be cut down to its first word.
reason: The 'from' value is PATO_0000946, which is plain oblong. The flora says oblong-lanceolate, so the lanceolate part is lost.
In the Flora of North America, Eriogonum plant size is given as height × width. 0.2–0.6 dm of height is 2–6 cm, which is what the annotation says.
'± black' means black with the 'approximately' qualifier, said of the paraphyses.
Homomallous moss leaves all turn toward one side. That is secund (one-sided) arrangement, which is a position value.

target: vascular bundle present, part of the angles of the perigynium (PO_0009044)
fix: In 'Perigynia ..., angles veined, faces veinless', the veins belong to the angles of the perigynium. The whole (perigynium) and the position (angles) must be kept. Otherwise 'veins present' has nothing to attach to, and it seems to contradict 'faces veinless'.
reason: The annotation says veins are present but drops that they are on the angles of the perigynia.
Leaflets somewhat pilose when young: pilose, with the young stage (PATO_0000309) kept as context.
Petals ovate to oblong: a range of shapes from ovate to oblong.
6–12 secondary veins on each side of the midvein. The count is per side, with the leaf midvein (PO_0020139) as the reference point.
The immature samara is a fruit, 2.4–3.7 cm long, with the immature state (PATO_0001501) kept.

target: leaf, middle and upper stem leaves: narrowly ovate | lanceolate | linear-lanceolate
fix: In 'Middle and upper stem leaves X, Y, or Z', the position (middle and upper stem leaves) must be kept. All the listed alternatives belong to the statement, and 'narrowly' changes the shape.
reason: The annotation says the whole taxon's leaves are ovate. The flora says this only of the middle and upper stem leaves (the lower leaves are described differently), says 'narrowly ovate', and lists lanceolate and linear-lanceolate as alternatives.

fix: In apocarpous flowers (Rosaceae, Ranunculaceae and others), a count of 'pistils' counts carpels. A flower has only one gynoecium, so a count over 1 cannot be about the gynoecium. The 'ca.' qualifier should also be kept.
reason: 'About 20 pistils in pistillate flowers' counts separate pistils, which are carpels. The context (pistillate flower) is right.

target: obovate to orbiculate-reniform (compound of orbicular PATO_0001934 and reniform PATO_0001871)
fix: A hyphenated shape such as 'orbiculate-reniform' is a blend of two shapes and must not be cut to its first part.
reason: The end of the range is orbiculate-reniform, but only orbicular was kept.
'Glandular-atomiferous' means covered with tiny sessile glands that look like specks. Gland-dotted fits, and it is said of the petioles.
'± glabrescent' stems: glabrescent with the 'approximately' qualifier.
A cypsela is a fruit. 'Glabrous or hirsute' are two alternative hair states.
'Petals much exceeding the stamens' means the petals are longer than the stamens.

fix: In a leaf-blade description, 'apex rounded' is about the apex. The bearer should be leaf apex, not the whole blade.
reason: Rounded fits obtuse (PATO_0001935, whose synonym is 'roundish'), but here it describes the leaf apex, not the whole lamina.
Stamens 3: count of 3.
Seeds numerous: seeds present, with the count word 'many'.
In grass descriptions, stem (culm) height is the plant's height. 1–5 dm is 10–50 cm.
Phyllaries lacking wings: winged, negated, on the involucral bract.
Corolla pink or pale purple: two alternative colours.
The corolla lobes are 1–3.5 mm wide. The lexicon has no corolla-lobe class, so petal is the accepted bearer for corolla lobes. The width is the lobes' width, not the tube's (1–3 mm).
